summary: This room is two subclusters stitched together by graph topology, not by theme: the palace's foundational meta trio (CLAUDE, ELDER, SCHEMA — Reference) and five Shop visualization Specialists (D3.js, LaTeX, Matplotlib, Mermaid, Observable Plot). The Shop tools are already densely and correctly cross-linked to each other (alternative-to / couples-with / enables chains that route briefs correctly), and the meta trio is already linked to itself — but I found no genuine bridge between the two halves; the meta docs never name a Shop tool and vice versa, so I'm not forcing one. The real finds were inside each half: a backwards `enables` link on Observable Plot (it claims to enable D3.js when its own prose says the opposite — Plot is built on D3, so D3 is the precondition), and a cluster of unsung wikilinks in ELDER and SCHEMA — Reference — dense reference prose that names entries (most usefully, the newcomer [[Agent Toolbox]], plus [[Palace Orchestrator]] and [[Entry Conatus]]) without carrying them into frontmatter.

typed_relations.label: built-on
typed_relations.rationale: Observable Plot's own frontmatter records itself as enabling D3.js, labeled 'built-on' — but the body says the opposite relationship: Plot is built ON D3, so D3 is the precondition, not Plot. The enables direction should point D3.js → Observable Plot.
typed_relations.evidence: Charter: "I refuse jobs that want custom interactive web viz... those route to [[D3.js]] (I'm built on D3; the escape hatch is always available)." Strengths: "Built on D3 — the escape hatch to full custom control is always available."
typed_relations.deep_pattern: A precondition link pointing away from its precondition — worth a general sweep for other 'built-on'/'underpins' labels that may share the same backwards pattern.

typed_relations.label: tool-tiers
typed_relations.rationale: ELDER's 'Age and its limits' section names the exact three-tier tool taxonomy (palace-reader / palace-writer / palace-orchestrator) that Agent Toolbox defines and owns, but the mention carries no frontmatter link. Agent Toolbox is also a priority newcomer (reached by only 2).
typed_relations.evidence: "a child that makes things keeps the tools its workshop needs; an elder is `palace-writer`, and an elder that dispatches others, `palace-orchestrator` ([[Agent Toolbox]])."
typed_relations.deep_pattern: ELDER states the age/tool-limit *principle*; Agent Toolbox is where that principle is actually mechanized into a roster. Fidelity test passed — this reasoning is specific to Agent Toolbox's actual profile table, not a generic 'see also.'

typed_relations.label: wire-for
typed_relations.rationale: §9 explicitly calls itself the spec and Palace Orchestrator the thing that executes it, with an imperative to read it first — a textbook enables relation (precondition → dependent), stated in the entry's own words but never wired into frontmatter.
typed_relations.evidence: "§4 types the edges between entries; §9 types the edges between agents ... This section is the wire; [[Palace Orchestrator]] is the executor. Read that before posting."

typed_relations.label: forward-vector-discipline
typed_relations.rationale: SCHEMA — Reference's own frontmatter-fields table sends the reader to Entry Conatus for the discipline of writing a forward_vector, but doesn't carry the link itself.
typed_relations.evidence: "The forward vector is the entry's articulated *conatus*: see [[Entry Conatus]] for the discipline of writing one."
